question: Should OpenClaw adopt gateway-local multi-user identity and exact-resource authorization as permanent core and Plugin SDK contracts for Workspaces sharing?
rationale: The branch is technically substantial but permanently changes identity, device admission, gateway roles, protocol data, persisted schemas, and public plugin APIs; automation cannot decide whether that product and trust model belongs in core.

options.title: Sponsor a staged core design
options.body: Approve the generic identity and authorization direction, require explicit contract and threat-model review, and split or gate implementation stages before merge.

options.title: Narrow to an external experiment
options.body: Keep the Teams portal and product workflow outside core while designing only the smallest generic plugin seam proven to be missing.

options.title: Keep OpenClaw single-operator
options.body: Decline the multi-user core direction and close the linked feature work while preserving the existing privileged dashboard model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged core design
recommendation.body: Approve the generic identity and authorization direction, require explicit contract and threat-model review, and split or gate implementation stages before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged and shaped the current Workspaces foundation and is the strongest available owner for deciding whether its core and Plugin SDK boundary should expand.
